reasons: Section 4.4 is the only clause granting the counterparty (Commerce One) inspection rights over our party's (Corio's) books, and it meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency capped at once per calendar year, inspections at reasonable times on reasonable notice, conducted by an independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, Commerce One bears all costs unless an underpayment exceeds 5%, and access is limited to books and records with no system or remote access.
No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is correct for a compliant finding; the deterministic frequency check also passes.

The rationale accurately identifies the only sub-preferred mechanics ('reasonable notice' rather than a quantified 30/15 days, and no express confidentiality undertaking for the auditor) and correctly treats them as minor sub-elements noted rather than deviations.
